speaker: YOU
text: [whispering, tense] It's two a.m. [pause] Why is my heart going this fast?

speaker: YOU
text: [faster, anxious] I have the meeting. And the rent. And I didn't answer her text. And—

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [softly, cutting in gently] Hey. Hey. You know this feeling.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Everyone does. Tight chest. Racing thoughts. That hum under everything.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: We even have one word for it.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Here's the strange part. A hundred years ago, if you'd told most doctors you were "stressed"... they'd have pictured a bridge.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Not a person. "Stress" was an engineering word. The load on a steel beam. The strain on a cable. [pause] Then one clumsy young scientist borrowed it... and gave it to all of us.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: And somebody paid for him to keep saying it.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [beat] This is the story of the man who invented stress. And why, the way you were taught about it... might be part of the problem.
